result.title: Beyond Modality Preference: Controlling Multimodal Arbitration under Modality Conflict in MLLMs
result.summary: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) integrate information across modalities, but become unreliable when those modalities disagree. Under conflicting inputs, MLLMs may favor modalities that are not the most reliable for the task, thus motivating inference-time control of modality arbitration. We identify a small set of attention heads, termed arbitration heads, that causally influence whether predictions follow visual or textual evidence. Building on this, we introduce a lightweight, training-free intervention that biases these heads toward a designated trusted modality at inference time. The identified heads are stable across calibration set sizes and generalize across settings, and steering them enables effective bidirectional control of modality reliance across diverse benchmarks. Our findings identify an effective control mechanism to align MLLM predictions with task-specified modality priorities. The code is available at https://github.com/zhaoyingpan/modality-arbitration.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究多模态大模型在视觉与文本证据冲突时如何仲裁模态，识别出少数因果影响预测偏向的「arbitration heads」，并提出无需训练的推理期干预，使模型转向指定可信模态。
AI.relevance_reason: 该工作直接关联 VLM 推理中是否使用视觉证据及视觉旁路问题，其因果头识别与推理期控制可供核查内部状态调控、证据筛选和模态贡献分配。
